title: Milestone cadence, embargo windows, and release-note delta automation for cross-team rollouts
creator: Asha Patel
description: Define and implement a coordinated milestone cadence and embargo-window policy across API, Console and Runtime teams; build a lightweight automation to extract release-note deltas from merged PRs, tag changes by customer-impact, and produce a canonical release notes draft for PM/Docs review. Deliverables include milestone calendar, embargo rules, release-note delta script (CI job), communication templates, and a short post-release monitoring checklist.
acceptance_criteria: Milestone calendar published with dates for scope lock, doc freeze, UI freeze, and production cutover
Embargo rules documented and approved by legal and comms (list of embargoed content and windows)
CI job that compiles merged PRs into a categorized delta file runs in the release branch and produces a candidate release notes draft
PM/Docs can review and finalize release notes within 48 hours of candidate draft
Automated notification (Slack/email) to stakeholders when draft is ready
Cross-team rollouts have gating metrics and assigned on-call owners for rollback/escalation
steps: Workshop with ENG/Console/Design/Docs/Comms to align on milestone cadence and freeze semantics
Draft embargo policy: acceptable content, exceptions, and handling of security fixes
Prototype a GitHub Actions job that aggregates merged PRs between last release tag and release branch and groups by label: feature, bug, docs, security, infra
Add PR labeling guidance to contributing docs and enforce via PR template
Build Slack notification to #release-ops and ping release owners with link to draft
Create release-note review rotation for PMs and Docs with 48-hour SLA
Define rollout gates: latency P90, error rate, and API success rate thresholds and canary volumes
Publish post-release monitoring checklist with owners and runbook links
decisions: Use PR labels (feature/bug/docs/security/infra) as primary taxonomy for release-note grouping
Embargo window is 48 hours pre-release for non-security customer-impacting content
Security fixes are allowed to bypass embargo with explicit security-approved blurb
Candidate release notes are generated automatically; human PM/Docs must sign off before public publishing
risks: Teams may not consistently apply PR labels leading to noisy candidate drafts
Late-breaking fixes post-embargo could require rushed comms; need clear exception path
Automation gaps if GitHub metadata is inconsistent across repos
Rollout gates might be insufficiently tuned causing false-positive rollbacks
